schema.note: Staging data for the episodes: who speaks, where the camera looks, where actors walk to, and the copy on the three balls. Nothing reads this file yet -- it is here so that the numbers a beat depends on live next to the scene that depends on them instead of only in a scene asset. Every position is in the slice_layout.json coordinate space.
schema.yWarning: The Y values below were taken from the nearest path control point in slice_layout.json, not resampled from terrain.heightField.grid. Snap them to the grid before trusting them; a marker 20cm under the cobbles is a camera that looks at the ground.

speakers.name: Linden
speakers.subtitle: Aster Field Lab
speakers.note: Named for the lime tree, following the series' habit of naming professors after plants, and matching a town named for a flower. Seventy-one, unhurried, and specific about paperwork -- the joke and the characterisation are the same thing: he is the person who believes writing it down is the work. DOES NOT EXIST IN THE LEVEL. slice_layout.json gameplay.npcs has no professor. He must be placed before any episode that names NPC_Professor can run.

requiredNpc.name: NPC_Professor
requiredNpc.positionNote: The far end of Path_TownLane_Lab, at the lab door, facing the same way as Town_Lab_01 (yaw 222) so he reads as having just come out of it. He is on the 45 deg camera axis with the dome behind him.

speakers.name: Kes
speakers.subtitle: Aster Town
speakers.note: Short for Kestrel. One syllable because he is interrupted constantly and the name plate has to survive being read forty times. He is Barry's function, not Barry: the momentum the player has not earned yet. He talks in three-word sentences when excited and complete ones when he has lost, which is the only characterisation the writing has room for.

speakers.name: Bram
speakers.subtitle: Aster Gate
speakers.existsAs: NPC_GateKeeper at (-9.6, 2.654, 0.4), yaw 150 -- standing at the head of the gate ramp, facing back down the street
speakers.note: MISMATCH: slice_layout.json gives this NPC displayName 'Townsfolk'. He carries the whole first act's gating and needs a name in the plate; either update the layout or let the dialogue's SpeakerName win over displayName. He is DP's mother-at-the-tall-grass and DP's route guard folded together.

speakers.name: Sela
speakers.subtitle: Aster Market
speakers.existsAs: NPC_Stallholder at (-13.6, 2.453, -12.2), yaw 8 -- market row, in the same shot as the spawn
speakers.note: Same displayName mismatch as Bram. Her only structural job is to answer 'what am I supposed to do' for a player who has been given control and no arrow.

speakers.name: Odell
speakers.subtitle: Town Gardens
speakers.note: Same displayName mismatch. Pure flavour, one line, and it is the only corroboration the bulletin gets.

speakers.name: Aster Field Lab
speakers.subtitle: Morning Bulletin
speakers.note: Speaks the opening bulletin without the player interacting with it -- it is playing to the empty plaza, which is the point. Tone System, so DialogueView renders it in the flat register rather than as a person.

markers.name: Look_LabDome
markers.note: CameraTo target for the first frame. Town_Lab_01 stands at (-1.453, 2.728, -5.691), 0.4m up and 8.8m tall, dead on the 45 deg camera axis from the player spawn; this marker is the dome itself at roughly 5.5m above its base. The fade-in reveals it already composed.

markers.name: Look_GateRamp
markers.note: Second control point of Path_GateRamp. Framing the ramp head with the two of them walking into it, so the drop is visible before Bram says anything about it.

markers.name: Look_RouteHead
markers.note: Bottom of the gate ramp / Spawn_RouteHead, lifted 1.5m so the flock has sky to go up into. The one shot in the opening that looks at the route.

markers.name: Look_GateStand
markers.note: Head height over the group standing at the top of the street. The default framing for everything spoken at the gate, including the rival battle.

markers.name: Look_Case
markers.note: The open case between Linden and the player, at chest height. The only close shot in the episode -- it exists so the three balls are the largest thing on screen at the moment of choosing.

markers.name: Look_LabDoor
markers.note: Linden in his own doorway with the dome above him. Deliberately rhymes with Look_LabDome from the first frame: the episode that opens the world is framed on the same building that opened the game.

markers.name: Mark_Rival_GateStand
markers.note: MoveActor destination for Kes. Just short of Bram, on Path_TownMain between (-9.6,-1.5) and (-8.2,1.0).

markers.name: Mark_Player_GateStand
markers.note: MoveActor destination for the player, ~2m behind Kes and facing north-east up the street. Roughly 9m of walk from the plaza spawn.

markers.name: Mark_Prof_Case
markers.note: Where Linden stops, behind and to the side of the player, having come up Path_TownMain from the lab lane junction near (-11.4,-5.0). ~11m of walk; the beat allows 6s and he should use most of it.

markers.name: Mark_Rival_GateWait
markers.note: Where Kes settles after the battle, at the very lip of the ramp, so he is the last thing in frame before the player descends. Conflicts with TrainerController.ReturnToPost -- see the beat note.

starterOptions.note: Copy for the three balls. The species ids are GAME ids from SliceRoster, verified against Assets/StreamingAssets/pokelab/species.json (Species[].Id / NameEn) and against the sprite cast in Tools/Sprites/species.py: game 1 = Bulbasaur (dex 1), game 5 = Charmander (dex 4), game 10 = Squirtle (dex 7). All three are in the 53-species sprite cast, so all three render. StarterSelection.cs already ships defaults; these are proposed replacements -- shorter, and written as a label on a ball rather than as a sentence about a type chart. The order matches SliceRoster.Starters, and each RivalCounterSpeciesId is the one Kes announces in op_choice_result_*.

options.Blurb: Grass · Poison — carries its own garden. Hard to finish.
Fire — thin early, frightening later. Keep the tail dry.
Water — steady, and forgiving of a bad first month.

signals.note: Ids raised through OverworldEvents.RaiseDialogueSignal by DialogueLine.EventId and DialogueChoice.ResultEventId. Every one of them is optional -- the scene plays without a listener, it just plays flatter.
signals.vfx.flock_startle: A dozen Pidgey out of the grass below the ramp, north over the gate. Prop/VFX work that does not exist. Pidgey is game id 21 and has a sprite, so a real flock is buildable rather than faked.
signals.story.case_open: The case opens: three balls, a light, a sting.
signals.story.dex_given: The item-get moment for the Pokédex. This is the loudest cue in the three episodes and should be the only one that stops the music.
signals.rival.answer.eager / rival.answer.dry: Cosmetic. Recorded only so a later scene could remember how the player answered.
